p0Matrix.why: Code cause fixed in B (every write path keeps unknown top-level + well-formed unknown ids; proven unit + Chromium). Remaining parts are deploy operations the diff cannot do: merge, a separate deploy before C, a soak so A tabs age out, and the rollback-floor rule.

The T1-vs-T2 loss happens inside C once C registers the key as known. #206 ships reusable helpers (unknownIdsIn, appendNew, KNOWN_SAVE_KEYS), but C must extend them. While the key is unknown to B, B keeps the whole array verbatim, so the risk does not exist between B and C.
#206 keeps schemaVersion 2 and does not bump. A v3 root is still erased by B on the first real write (S4). 'No bump' remains a constraint on C.
OWNED => UNLOCKED grandfathering is C logic. B's Shop can still buy known ingredients without a fee during a rollback window, which makes I-1 in C more necessary.
Single-key/single-setItem is kept by writeSave, but a stale B tab can revert C's fee payment (pitzBalance) while keeping the entitlement (S3b).
B keeps unknown-recipe ledger ids, so a ledger C saturates with future ids survives a B write. Known-id ledger ids are already kept by A. Saturation itself (3-4C) is not in #206.
3-state vs 5-state cutover is an Owner Decision (OD-SM-1). Save-layer code cannot settle it.

rollbackFloor.beforeAnyCDeploy: A (main dff233c) is a safe target from B: for a save with no unknown data B writes byte-for-byte what A writes (S6: identical bytes after boot, pizza, Shop and Lunch Rush writes; 2430/2430 vitest pass on the merged tree).
rollbackFloor.afterCDeployed: B (a build containing #206's writeSave) is the floor. Any build without it (A, a revert of #206, or a workflow_dispatch of an older SHA) erases C data on its first write, including the EP4 boot write. B cannot restore it afterwards (S3d).
rollbackFloor.staleTabs: A tabs opened before B's deploy behave like a rollback to A (S3e). The app has no service worker or forced-reload mechanism, so only time (soak) reduces this.
